thread.title: Chip makers lead European stocks higher after AMS reports 252% jump in revenue - MarketWatch

author: Sara Sjolin
title: Chip makers lead European stocks higher after AMS reports 252% jump in revenue - MarketWatch
text:
European stocks ended a volatile session in negative territory on Monday, with losses for banks and commodity companies outweighing a rally for chip makers that came after Apple-supplier AMS AG reported a major jump in revenue and lifted its sales forecasts.
What are markets doing?
The Stoxx Europe 600 index SXXP, -0.19% fell 0.2% to close at 399.79, paring back after a 0.5% gain on Friday.
Germany’s DAX 30 index DAX, -0.12% slipped 0.1% to 13,324.48, while France’s CAC 40 index PX1, -0.14% gained 0.1% to 5,521.59. The U.K.’s FTSE 100 index UKX, +0.08% picked up 0.1% to 7,671.53 .
The euro EURUSD, -0.4185% dropped to $1.2347 from $1.2427 late Friday in New York, while the pound GBPUSD, -0.6638% pulled back to $1.4032 from $1.4160. Both currencies rallied last week, as the dollar suffered a significant setback after U.S. Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin said a weaker greenback is good for U.S. trade.

What is driving the market?
With little on the economic calendar, traders instead focused on corporate news and particularly on an update from AMS AG AMS, +16.92% AMSSY, +19.15% The Austrian chip company said its fourth-quarter revenues soared 252% , helping full-year 2017 revenue come in at a record €1.06 billion.
AMS, whose sensor technology helps power the Apple AAPL, -1.56% iPhone X’s facial-recognition feature, also lifted its revenue forecast for 2016-2019 to compound annual growth of 60%. Shares surged 17%, leading the Stoxx 600. The Stoxx Europe 600 Technology Index FX8, +0.48% climbed 0.4%.
Oil companies, however, weighed on the markets, as crude prices CLH8, -0.94% tanked 1.4%. The Stoxx Europe 600 Oil & Gas Index SXEP, -0.60% lost 0.6%.
Which stocks are in focus?
The gain for AMS helped power other chip makers. Shares of Dialog Semiconductor PLC DLG, +3.06% ended up 1.5% and STMicroelectronics NV STM, +2.39% rose 2.4%.
Shares of Anglo American PLC AAL, +1.23% gained 1.2% after the miner said it has sold the New Largo thermal-coal project and Old New Largo closed coal mine in South Africa for 850 million rand ($71.5 million) in cash.
Shares of Sanofi SA SAN, -0.79% SNY, -1.18% slipped 0.8% after the French drug giant said it’s buying biopharmaceutical company Ablynx NV ABLX, +18.53% for about €3.9 billion.
Getinge AB GETIB, -10.46% slumped 10.5%. The Swedish medical technology company said full-year underlying earnings were “not satisfactory” and that it will now gradually reduce operating expenses.
Shares of Bankia SA BKIA, -4.31% lost 4.3% after the Spanish bank swung to a loss in the fourth quarter.
What are strategists saying?
“Although U.K. and European markets have faced some currency headwinds recently, more generally global equity markets continue to hit new highs, as the fear of missing out has escalated and a tidal wave of new money combined with a surge in M&A activity has seen share prices increase sharply,” said Rebecca O’Keeffe, head of investment at Interactive Investor, in a note.
“The acceleration of share price rises has caught even prominent bulls by surprise as each day adds to equity valuations and raises suggestions that the market may be entering a late-cycle surge,” she added.
